reviews.detail: Real-phone WP-015C acceptance found that the completed solid trajectory line overlaid the cast/impact presentation, while Needlepoint and Spoolburst lacked a discrete in-flight visual. The scoped repair removes the completed trajectory line, retains the dashed aim guide, and renders compact procedural projectile/impact visuals for the two unapproved Relic families. The focused re-check then found that Threadball retained one short gold line below the first projectile: its intended blue tail was overdrawn by a gold segment. The final in-scope correction removes that segment and narrows the source-free effect grammar to a blue-only short tail. The next real-phone check found that the large shared Wizard's visible upper body is outside the v1/v2 lower-body direct-hit target. The project owner authorized the bounded v3 correction: new challenges use a fixed body profile (`halfWidth: 32`, `top: 85`, `bottom: 13`) for direct projectile contact; v1/v2 replay behavior remains immutable. The project owner subsequently tested the hitbox on phone and accepted it; the focused Ubuntu replacement was explicitly waived.

The permanent Loomseed removed the former empty-hand socket preservation requirement, so one free-tier Custom idle pilot was authorized from exact approved combined presentation master 1CC252B45C93D2553AC733DAA6AA49D05D6351DCC85E61EA559ECED458C9419C. Its 25-frame result retains a small focus but fails the still-required Wizard face identity: it replaces both black bead eyes and the stitched mouth with one large cartoon eye/no mouth. The old raw-empty-palm pilots and this combined-presentation pilot are rejected. No paid control, retry, normalizer, staging, runtime path, or asset promotion is authorized.

The official BFL FLUX MCP connector was registered globally at https://mcp.bfl.ai and completed OAuth login. BFL documents it as an OAuth FLUX.2 image connector, so it is intentionally separate from the direct FLUX 3 API key lane. No source image/video was uploaded. The documented BFL API training-use terms require a subsequent owner decision before the first limited image-to-video pilot.
